text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm updating the "Territory availability" doc for a couple of customers in LATAM and SEA. Need help finalizing the data-jurisdiction note and an SDK snippet showing how to pass a regional preference header. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 :link:

alex: looking now, thanks. question: legal wants us to avoid "data never leaves X" phrasing. Can we say "processed in preferred region where possible" instead? :thinking_face:

jia: +1 to alex. For private deployments we should call out the KMS/HSM footnote. Also suggest adding a short table of which countries map to which region labels (e.g., BR -> latam, SG -> sea) rather than long prose.

sanjay: I can help map the country -> region list. Tiny nit: the header name we use in the SDK snippet should match runtime routing. We landed on `X-Region-Preference` in the routing spec, right?

maria: yes @sanjay — runtime teams confirmed `X-Region-Preference`. We'll surface that as an optional hint (not an SLA). Add a short cURL + JS SDK example below. Can someone double-check wording for the residency footnote? Here's the proposed language:

"Data residency is expressed as a preferred processing location. Requests may be routed to alternative compatible regions when capacity or compliance constraints require it. For sensitive workloads, use Redwood Private or Dedicated to ensure customer-managed controls and explicit locality."

alex: wording looks good to me. maybe replace "compatible regions" with "fallback regions" so it's clearer.

maria: updated. Anyone from legal to ack the footnote? @sara-legal ? :eyes:

sara-legal: acked. prefer we add a parenthetical linking to the privacy page: (see Policies > Data Residency). I'll post the URL in the PR comments.

docs-bot: Pull request opened by maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 — labels: docs, region-availability, needs-review

jia: SDK snippet (JS) — short, copyable. Feel free to paste into the PR:

```js
// set a preferred region hint for routing
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const res = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'redwood-mini',
  input: 'Summarize this document',
  headers: { 'X-Region-Preference': 'latam' }
});
console.log(res.output_text);
```

and cURL:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
     -H "X-Region-Preference: sea" \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","input":"Hello"}'
```

maria: perfect — I'll add those snippets, the country->region mini-table, and the legal link. I'll also mark the PR for backport to the 2.1 sidebar since this clarifies routing for older SDKs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
